title: BERTDetect: A Neural Topic Modelling Approach for Android Malware Detection
read_from: arXiv preprint (published version: ACM WWW 2025 companion)
subcategory: security: topic clusters of app descriptions for malware outlier detection
task: Unsupervised Android malware detection from app descriptions and API usage
problem: Prior description-based detectors (LDA + k-means, CHABADA) do not capture the semantics of app descriptions, which limits outlier detection.
architecture: BERTopic (BERT embeddings -> UMAP -> HDBSCAN -> class-based TF-IDF) clusters benign app descriptions into functionality topics; apps are assigned by topic affinity; one One-Class SVM per topic is trained on sensitive API calls; new apps are flagged as malware when their API use is an outlier for their topic.
llm_or_encoder: BERT sentence embeddings (via BERTopic); baseline G-CATA uses OpenAI ada embeddings

datasets.name: AndroCatSet
datasets.details: 5,000 benign Google Play apps in 50 categories plus 448 malicious apps with retrieved descriptions; train 4000 benign, validation and test 724 apps each

key_results: F1 0.54 vs 0.49 for G-CATA (about 10% relative gain); TP rate 50.89% vs 42.86%.
About 70% of BERTopic topics have NPMI above 0.2, compared with about 40% for LDA and 0% for CHABADA.
strengths: Shows that higher topic coherence translates into better downstream detection.
Lightweight: uses app metadata rather than code or runtime analysis.

limitations.text: Evaluated on a single dataset (AndroCatSet); few datasets contain both APKs and descriptions.
Metadata-based signals are weaker than code-level or runtime analysis and are meant to complement them.
